svg.title: Formalism numerical witness workbench
svg.desc: All typed deterministic numerical witnesses are plotted from their declared schemas with residual, tolerance, theorem-mirror, unit, and boundary summaries. The visible boundary label identifies these diagnostics as non-proof evidence.
svg.text: 22 typed witnesses · 22 formal families · exact evaluated schemas
Deterministic numerical witnesses are explanatory non-proof evidence. They can expose finite sign, normalization, support, rank,
identity, and contraction errors; they are neither Lean proof receipts nor empirical validation of the Free Energy Principle.

g.title: Exact Boltzmann EFE floor, perception chain rule, and affinity-bounded gain · boltzmann-efe-affinity-gap · standalone-efe-formalizations
g.desc: the KL-regularized EFE objective attains exactly the inverse-precision log-partition floor at the Boltzmann control posterior with inverse-precision KL gaps, the perception channel splits the belief information gap exactly into outcome-marginal plus posterior-averaged parts without increasing it, and the two-state epistemic gain is the relaxation-decaying KL bounded by the affinity production rate, and the law-weighted reversible/circulation split is unique: the t-0060 datum's constraint-satisfying split is exactly the canonical symmetricPart/circulationPart pair, a p-reversible field has the split (W, 0), and the forward circulation 1/2 with reverse entry -1/4 is genuinely nonzero and strictly negative Boundary: At time zero the identity kernel returns the full belief gap 0.0610605352, the squared-relaxation envelope 0.1071428571 stays loose by 0.0460823220, and the affinity bound 0.1330954793 leaves slack 0.0720349441. The law-weighted datum splits canonically, its competing pair is unique on the step-1/4 grid, and the reversible datum W_rev = [[1, 4], [2, 3]] carries the split (W, 0). g.aria-label: Skew cancellations, three-term expansion remainder, and the failing unconditional solenoidal drop, accepted, Theorem Instance
g.title: Skew cancellations, three-term expansion remainder, and the failing unconditional solenoidal drop · geometric-solenoidal-drop · geometric-mechanics-notation
g.desc: the skew trace and quadratic cancellations hold exactly on the symmetry hypotheses, the symmetrized discrete Hessian is symmetric and coincides with symmetric data, the expansion remainder slot evaluates to exactly 1 on the concrete derivative datum, and the honesty-guard candidate current (0, -1) has node divergence (1, -1) so the unconditional solenoidal drop fails; symmetrization is the unique Frobenius least-squares projection (exact Pythagoras, minimality with equality exactly at the symmetrizer, residual 1/2 on the nonsymmetric datum), and the uncancelled remainder obeys the squared Cauchy-Schwarz budget with equality attained on aligned data and gap 1 on the pinned remainderG datum Boundary: On the honesty guard the transport divergence is (2, -2) at the two nodes and the candidate current (0, -1) has node divergence 1 at node 0: the drop fails, matching the compiled witness. The Frobenius projection residual is exactly 1/2 on the nonsymmetric datum, the budget is attained on the aligned gradient (1, 0), and the pinned remainderG = (1, 1) datum stays strict with gap 1. g.aria-label: Finite Bernoulli posterior reconstruction, accepted, Theorem Instance
g.title: Finite Bernoulli posterior reconstruction · core-bernoulli-bayes-reconstruction · core-bayesian-mechanics
g.desc: At nonzero evidence the posterior atom equals prior times likelihood divided by evidence. Boundary: All-zero likelihood gives zero evidence, so no posterior division is attempted. A normalized likelihood-only value 0.9 differs from the first actual posterior and is not silently treated as Bayes with a nonuniform prior. Theorem mirrors: fep_fep045.FEP045.fep045_bernoulli_posterior_closed, fep_fep045.FEP045.fep045_posterior_mass_one Formal alignment: theorem_instance. g.title: Interior Bernoulli expected-score Fisher metric · core-bernoulli-fisher-interior · core-information-geometry
g.desc: For 0 < p < 1, expected score is 0 and Fisher information is 1/(p(1-p)); a nonzero tangent has positive metric. Boundary: Both singular endpoints are refused by the existing Bernoulli Fisher helper. No zero/infinite endpoint metric or general multidimensional statistical Fisher claim is plotted. Theorem mirrors: fep_fep038.FEP038.fep038_expectedScore_zero, fep_fep038.FEP038.fep038_fisherInformation_eq, fep_fep038.FEP038.fep038_fisherMetric_pos Formal alignment: theorem_instance. g.title: Binary Shannon entropy maximum in nats · core-binary-entropy-maximum · core-thermodynamics
g.desc: For sampled probability parameters, entropy is bounded by log(2) nats and peaks at one half. Boundary: Negative mass is refused by the existing finite-law numerical helper. This is the probability-domain Bernoulli theorem, not general constrained MaxEnt or Real.binEntropy's total extension outside [0, 1]. Theorem mirrors: fep_fep030.FEP030.fep030_binaryEntropy_max, fep_fep030.FEP030.fep030_binaryEntropy_eq_max_iff Formal alignment: theorem_instance. Typed checks: entropy-bound: ge(0.0, 0.0), tolerance 1e-12, residual 0.0, accepted; fair-attainment: eq(0.0, 0.0), tolerance 1e-12, residual 0.0, accepted; offuniform-strict: predicate(True, True), tolerance 0.0, residual 0.0, accepted; invalid-probability-refusal: predicate(True, True), tolerance 0.0, residual 0.0, accepted.
